audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says 'never waste both CC tools on a CC-immune target', mid says 'Never commit your Pillar or Subjugate while his R icon is glowing', spikes[1] says 'never drop Pillar or Subjugate while his R is active or both abilities are wasted', and wants.foe[1] has Olaf popping Ragnarok to neutralise both at once.
audit.why: Subjugate is not crowd control. Riot: 'Trundle immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance.' Ragnarok grants immunity to disables — there is nothing in a stat theft for that immunity to stop, so Subjugate lands through it. Worse for Olaf, Ragnarok 'passively gains increased armor and magic resist', which means the ultimate he presses to escape Trundle is adding to the pile Subjugate takes a percentage of. The entry is telling the player to hold their best ability for the exact moment it is worth the most.
audit.corrected: Subjugate is a stat theft, not a disable, so it lands straight through Ragnarok — and Ragnarok's own passive Armor and MR are part of what you take.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (R Ragnarok: passive armor and magic resist, activate for immunity to disables)

audit.whatIsWrong: True damage is attributed to his autos and to his ultimate: early says 'his lifesteal and true-damage autos', whys[1] says he 'weaves true-damage autos', wants.foe[2] says 'his true-damage autos out-trade your pattern', and spikes[1] says 'Ragnarok makes him CC-immune AND deals true damage'. Berserker Rage is never named.
audit.why: The true damage is Reckless Swing, a single 325-range ability on 11/10/9/8/7 that costs Olaf health and refunds it if it kills — not his attacks, and nothing in Ragnarok's text mentions damage of any kind. Meanwhile the passive that actually shapes the fight is missing: Berserker Rage gives him attack speed AND lifesteal scaled to his MISSING health, so a low Olaf swings faster and heals harder. That reverses the usual read on an extended trade — Trundle's plan of grinding him down makes him stronger the closer it gets to working.
audit.corrected: The true damage is Reckless Swing (E), 11s at rank 1 from 325, and it costs him health. Berserker Rage scales his attack speed and lifesteal off his MISSING health, so a low Olaf is a faster Olaf.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (P Berserker Rage; E Reckless Swing, cd 11/10/9/8/7, range 325, trueDamage; R Ragnarok)

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow is described only as an axe that 'slows and deals flat damage'. early says 'do not burn Pillar just to delay his retrieve — save it for a real pattern'.
audit.why: Two things are missing and they point the opposite way. Undertow reduces ARMOUR as well as move speed, so the axe is not just chip — it is softening Trundle for everything that follows. And 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is RESET', so his 9-second flat cooldown is only nine seconds when he cannot reach the axe. Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain, so a pillar dropped between Olaf and his thrown axe forces him to walk the long way round for the reset. Delaying the retrieve is not a waste of Pillar; it is the only thing in Trundle's kit that touches his early engine.
audit.corrected: Undertow strips Armor as well as move speed, and picking the axe up resets its flat 9s outright. Pillar of Ice between Olaf and the axe makes him walk around for it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (Q Undertow, cd 9, range 1000, 'reducing their Armor and Move Speed', 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset')
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, impassable terrain)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere in either layer. whys[3] and whys[4] describe the level-6 all-in as a coin flip decided by 'whose cooldown is up' without giving either.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80 and Subjugate is 120/100/80. His is back first at ranks 1 and 2 by twenty and ten seconds, and they level out only at rank 3 — so the coin flip is weighted his way for most of the game, which is a different instruction from 'track it better than he does'. The other clause that matters is that Ragnarok's immunity lasts 'for as long as he keeps attacking', so it is not a fixed duration: breaking contact ends it, and Pillar's slow starts applying again.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok 100/90/80 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — his is up first at ranks 1 and 2. Its immunity lasts only while he keeps attacking, so breaking contact ends it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (R cd 100/90/80, 'immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking')

audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] reads Olaf while whys[6] under it says 'you out-duel Olaf decisively in any extended side-lane fight' and late opens 'Two items in and the matchup resolves in your favour for good'. win[5] reads Olaf while whys[5] describes a knife-edge with no clean advantage either way.
audit.why: The packet has 51.21% over 248 games, a small Trundle lean, and the entry's own two-item paragraph is the most confident sentence in the whole file. Labelling that stage Olaf contradicts it outright. The early stages the chart gives Olaf are correct — Undertow's resetting 9s and 1000 range against a 300-range bite is a real kite pattern.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-3 Olaf; Levels 4-6 Skill; first item Skill; two-plus items Trundle. win[5] should read Skill and win[6] should read Trundle.

edits.before: Olaf's thrown axes are the whole early story — each one slows and deals flat damage, and at levels 1-3 you have no reliable way to close on him before he kites out. He wins level 1 by hurling an axe the instant he retrieves it, keeping you in range of a slow without stepping into Chomp range; do not trade auto-for-auto into his axe pattern. At level 2 he can retrieve the axe and reset the slow in one smooth motion, making the short-trade window he creates genuinely punishing before your Frozen Domain is even on the ground. Level 3 he completes the kit and has the durability to just stand in your face and out-sustain — his lifesteal and true-damage autos mean you cannot bleed him out either. Farm safely, hold the wave on your side, and do not burn Pillar just to delay his retrieve — save it for a real pattern.
edits.after: Olaf's thrown axes are the whole early story, and they do more than slow: Undertow strips Armor as well as move speed, and picking the axe back up RESETS its flat 9s outright. He wins level 1 by throwing the instant he retrieves, holding you in the slow from 1000 without ever entering Chomp's 300. That reset is his engine, so Pillar of Ice between him and the thrown axe is real value — impassable terrain means he walks the long way round for it. Level 3 he completes the kit and can stand in your face: Berserker Rage scales his attack speed and lifesteal off his MISSING health, so a low Olaf is a faster Olaf, and Reckless Swing is flat true damage on an 11s that costs him health he refunds on a kill. Farm safely and hold the wave on your side.

edits.before: From levels 4-5 onward the window starts to even out as your Chomp ranks up and the AD steal becomes meaningful every trade — but Ragnarok is now online and that changes everything. Never commit your Pillar or Subjugate while his R icon is glowing; bait it first by stepping up aggresively, then back off, let him pop it chasing, and immediately run your full pattern the moment the CC-immunity expires. Inside Frozen Domain with Ragnarok down you absolutely win the extended trade — W gives you the speed to stick, Chomp bleeds his AD every auto, and he has no true-damage output without the constant R uptime. Level 6 is even with a slight lean toward Skill: Subjugate is online but so is Ragnarok, and whichever of you manages the cooldown tracking better takes the all-in.
edits.after: From levels 4-5 onward the window starts to even out as Chomp ranks and the AD sap bites every trade — but Ragnarok is online at 100/90/80 against your 120/100/80, so his ultimate is back first at ranks 1 and 2. Read what it actually does. It passively grants him Armor and MR, and on cast it makes him immune to disables only for as long as he keeps attacking. So Pillar of Ice loses its slow while its terrain still stands, and breaking contact ends the immunity — while Subjugate is a stat theft rather than a disable, so it lands straight through, taking a slice of the very Armor and MR his ultimate gave him. Level 6 leans Skill: both ultimates are live, and the better cooldown tracker takes the all-in.

edits.before: Two items in and the matchup resolves in your favour for good — Subjugate strips enough armor and MR from Olaf mid-fight that even his true-damage autos do not keep pace with what you drain back, and Trinity Force Spellblade procs off every Chomp mean the burst in each trade cycle is yours. He remains dangerous if you fight with Subjugate on cooldown or outside Frozen Domain — those two mistakes cost you even at full build — but if you respect the cooldown window and force the fight on your own ice you out-duel him cleanly. Split-push with Frozen Domain keeping you perpetually faster in the side lane; no one chases you off a tower once you have two items.
edits.after: Two items in and the matchup resolves in your favour for good — Subjugate takes a percentage of Olaf's Health, Armor and MR, Ragnarok's passive resists included, and doubles the theft across four seconds while Trinity Force procs off every Chomp. He stays dangerous if you fight with Subjugate down or off your ice, and Berserker Rage means the lower he drops the faster he swings, so finish the job rather than kite it. Respect the cooldown window, force the fight on your own ice, and you out-duel him cleanly. Split-push with Frozen Domain keeping you perpetually faster; nobody chases you off a tower at two items.

notes: BIGGEST CORRECTION: four separate strings tell the player to hold Subjugate while Ragnarok is up, on the grounds that Olaf is 'CC-immune'. Subjugate is not crowd control — it is a stat theft — so the immunity has nothing to stop, and Ragnarok 'passively gains increased armor and magic resist', meaning the ultimate he presses is adding to the pile Subjugate takes a percentage of. The entry was withholding Trundle's best ability at the exact moment it pays most. Ragnarok's immunity also lasts only 'for as long as he keeps attacking', so it is not a fixed duration and breaking contact ends it — Pillar's slow starts applying again. SECOND CORRECTION: true damage attributed to his autos in three strings and to Ragnarok in a fourth. It is Reckless Swing, one ability, 11s at rank 1 from 325 range, and it costs him health. Berserker Rage — absent from both layers — is what actually shapes the fight: attack speed and lifesteal scaled to his MISSING health, so grinding him low makes him faster, which is the opposite of what an extended Frozen Domain trade assumes. THIRD: Undertow reduces ARMOUR as well as move speed, and its flat 9s RESETS when he picks the axe up. The entry said 'do not burn Pillar just to delay his retrieve' — but the retrieve is the reset, and Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, so putting it between Olaf and his axe is the only thing in Trundle's kit that touches his early engine. I reversed that instruction. COOLDOWNS: Ragnarok 100/90/80 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — his back first at ranks 1 and 2, level only at rank 3, which weights the 'coin flip' the entry describes. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Ragnarok's disable immunity covers slows specifically, and whether Pillar of Ice's terrain can be walked over by anything in his kit — his kit lists no dash, and the needsResearch block is empty, so I described the terrain as forcing a longer walk rather than as an absolute block. NOT EDITED (enum): win[6] reads Olaf directly above a whys[6] saying 'you out-duel Olaf decisively' and a late paragraph opening 'the matchup resolves in your favour for good'; win[5] reads Olaf above a why describing a knife-edge. Those should read Trundle and Skill.
